reason: आदाब अर्ज़ है, मिज़ाज शरीफ़? is an ornate courtly Urdu greeting no learner will ever use or hear in everyday Hindi; replaced with the everyday greeting.

target: बेशक, तुम मेरे साथ चल सकते हो।
english: Of course, you can come with me.
reason: मेहनत रंग लाई is a proverb-style motto, and बेशक sits oddly in front of it; the new sentence keeps बेशक doing its real job in ordinary speech.

target: यह काम मुझे ही करना पड़ेगा।
english: I'll have to do this work myself.
reason: यह काम मुझसे ही होगा is unnatural and boastful; the natural use of this frame is मुझसे यह नहीं होगा, so the emphatic ही is kept in a sentence people actually say.

target: मेरे पड़ोसी हमारी बहुत मदद करते हैं।
english: My neighbours help us a lot.
reason: Padded description ('very kind and helpful person') that states nothing usable; replaced with a concrete everyday statement using the same possessive frame.

target: मेरी सास बहुत अच्छी हैं और हमारे साथ रहती हैं।
english: My mother-in-law is very nice and lives with us.
reason: Vacuous double-adjective filler plus the bookish tag महिला; the replacement keeps the possessive + honorific plural but adds real information.

target: मेरे कॉलेज में कई अच्छे दोस्त हैं।
english: I have many good friends at my college.
reason: 'in my life' is greeting-card padding; anchoring the same X में … कई … हैं pattern to a real place makes it a sentence someone would actually say.

target: बस अड्डा स्टेशन से ज़्यादा पास है।
english: The bus stand is closer than the station.
reason: से नज़दीक reads as 'near to the station', not the comparative the English claims; ज़्यादा makes the comparison explicit and natural.
